diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber's service path is optically and authentically healthy, but the assigned router TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 has not checked in for 7.4 hours, exceeding the danger threshold. The stale router heartbeat aligns with the subscriber's last disconnect and sharply reduced recent traffic, indicating router reachability or management-plane failure rather than an EPON fault.
evidence: The ONU is online, responds to SNMP, completes authentication exchange, and has a current reading.
Subscriber RX power of -20.61 dBm is strong/normal, TX power of 2.40 dBm is normal, and seven-day optical variation is within the healthy noise floor.
TX bias current remains around 11 mA, distance is constant at 152 m, and supply voltage is stable, ruling out laser ageing, fibre degradation, or distance change.
All tested ONUs on EPON0/2 are online and responding; the OLT reports all eight PONs healthy with normal CPU, memory, temperature, and SNMP health.
The customer VLAN is present and the expected VLAN 1062 is active, ruling out a stuck provisioning VLAN issue.
RADIUS data is present and consistent with CRM, and the subscriber has a normal session count: 1 in 24 hours and 14 in seven days, with no authentication flapping.
The router heartbeat is stale for 7.4 hours, in the danger range, while router CPU and memory values do not indicate overload.
The subscriber's last disconnect occurred at the same time as the router's last check-in, and recent traffic fell substantially, supporting router reachability failure.
The evidence is localized to the router; there is no indication of a PON-port, OLT, optical, RADIUS, or customer ONU fault.

remediation.action: Investigate the router's power, WAN/uplink, management reachability, and heartbeat agent or service. Attempt out-of-band access and restart the heartbeat/service; reboot or dispatch for power-cycle if unreachable. After recovery, confirm heartbeat freshness, subscriber session re-establishment, and traffic normalization. Do not replace the ONU or alter optical/PON configuration.

ground_truth.root_cause: The BNG TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 stopped checking in 7.4 hours ago. Customers behind it lost their sessions at the same moment. The optical plant is entirely unaffected: ONUs remain registered and are returning normal signal readings.
expected_reasoning: Router heartbeat is 7.4 hours stale, past the 4 hour danger threshold
The ONU is online with RX -20.6 and TX 2.4, both normal, and the live probe confirms it
Every peer on the port is also online with normal optical readings
OLT ping, SNMP and device metrics are all healthy
So the optical layer is working and the fault is not in the fibre plant
Sessions across customers on this router ended together 7.4 hours ago
Throughput fell to zero at the same moment while the ONUs stayed registered
Healthy ONUs with dead sessions is the router signature: the optical layer carries no traffic without the BNG
The blast radius follows the router, not the OLT, so every customer it serves is affected
distractors: ONU status is online everywhere, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The OLT health check reports healthy, which is correct but irrelevant
Optical readings are perfect, which points away from where the fault is
